Must Have: Understands how to define database tables, columns, and relationships.
Desirable: Designs normalized schemas that ensure data integrity and efficiency.
Advanced/ Best: Creates scalable, flexible schemas that support evolving business requirements and high throughput.

Must Have: Can create simple ER diagrams showing relationships between entities.
Desirable: Designs complex ER models with one-to-many and many-to-many relationships.
Advanced/ Best: Optimizes ER models for large-scale systems, applying abstraction and inheritance patterns effectively.

Topics: Different types of Keys and Constraints
Must Have: Understands primary, foreign, and unique keys and basic constraints.
Desirable: Applies composite keys, check constraints, and cascading rules properly.
Advanced/ Best: Designs constraint strategies to enforce data quality and optimize referential integrity at scale.

Must Have: Understands normalization forms and applies them to remove redundancy.
Desirable: Balances normalization and denormalization for performance and reporting.
Advanced/ Best: Designs hybrid models using controlled denormalization to optimize read/write trade-offs.

Must Have: Understands what a transaction is and its importance for data consistency.
Desirable: Implements multi-step transactional operations with rollback capabilities.
Advanced/ Best: Designs high-throughput transactional systems with reliable transaction isolation and recovery mechanisms.

Must Have: Knows and explains Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability concepts.
Desirable: Designs operations ensuring ACID compliance for complex transactions.
Advanced/ Best: Tunes ACID properties for scalability, implementing distributed or eventual consistency where appropriate.

Must Have: Understands how database locks prevent conflicting operations.
Desirable: Manages isolation levels to balance consistency and concurrency.
Advanced/ Best: Optimizes concurrency control strategies for high-load OLTP systems using row-level and optimistic locking.

Must Have: Proficient in SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, subqueries, basic window functions
Creates simple indexes to speed up lookups and joins.
Desirable: Designs compound and covering indexes for query optimization.
Advanced/ Best: Implements adaptive and partial indexing strategies tuned to query workload patterns.

Must Have: Reads basic execution plans to identify full scans and join types.
Desirable: Interprets plans to pinpoint performance bottlenecks and inefficiencies.
Advanced/ Best: Optimizes complex queries using advanced plan tuning and cost-based optimization techniques.

Must Have: Understands what partitioning and sharding are conceptually.
Desirable: Applies partitioning to improve performance and manage large tables.
Advanced/ Best: Designs scalable sharding and distributed partitioning architectures for global OLTP systems.

Topics: Understands SQL, NoSQL and their use cases
Must Have: Knows the differences between SQL and NoSQL systems.
Desirable: Selects appropriate data storage systems based on workload and schema flexibility.
Advanced/ Best: Designs polyglot persistence architectures combining SQL and NoSQL for optimal performance and scalability.

Must Have: Applies schema changes using manual SQL scripts.
Desirable: Uses migration tools (e.g., Alembic, Flyway, Liquibase) for version control.
Advanced/ Best: Designs automated migration workflows with rollback and CI/CD integration for zero-downtime releases.

Topics: Data Migration (transferring data across environments and systems)
Must Have: Performs basic data exports and imports between environments.
Desirable: Automates data migration with validation and transformation logic.
Advanced/ Best: Designs large-scale, reliable migration strategies supporting incremental loads and schema evolution.
